MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps / Platform Engineering | QA Automation Engineer
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with experience owning CI/CD pipelines and automating test infrastructure for three product teams. Built short-lived merge-request environments using Helm and Kubernetes, and improved pipeline speed and reliability through parallelisation and dependency caching. Personal infrastructure projects include a k3s homelab with GitOps, monitoring and Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS infrastructure. Currently studying for the Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) exam.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure and delivery: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level experience), k3s, Argo CD
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform (personal project), Ansible (basic), Bash, Python
Monitoring and data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL, GitLab API
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Systems and networking: Linux, Traefik ingress, TLS certificate automation with cert-manager
Languages: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL
Cloud learning: AWS fundamentals (EC2 and S3, personal learning); Hetzner VPS (personal project)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by profiling pipelines, parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; monthly CI runner costs decreased by about 30%.
- Built short-lived merge-request test environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data; they are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding and created Grafana dashboards to report flaky tests by team.
- Wrote an internal guide to the CI system used in team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Performed manual and automated testing of web and mobile applications for client projects.
- Introduced a Selenium and Java automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node k3s cluster using Raspberry Pi 5 devices, with applications deployed from a Git repository through Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Automated deployment of a separate, short-lived environment for every merge request using GitLab CI and Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster.
- Enabled QA and product teams to review features before merge and run end-to-end tests against each environment.
- Configured automatic environment removal after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and separated end-to-end tests into a dedicated stage.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.

Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health | 2023
- Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and created Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team.
- Supported teams in identifying recurring failures; the flaky-test rate fell from 7% to below 1%.

EDUCATION
BEng Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation | Exam booked for January 2027

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into DevOps/platform engineering. The Professional Summary is focused, and the experience and project sections use specific technologies, ownership language, and quantified results. The strongest evidence includes reducing pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, reducing runner costs by approximately 30%, operating ephemeral environments for three teams, and reducing flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The document is professional and credible, and it appropriately qualifies Terraform, AWS, Kubernetes, and CKA preparation rather than overstating them. The main limitation is that the CV presents mostly CI/test infrastructure and personal cloud infrastructure experience, whereas the target role is centered on production cloud infrastructure, Terraform/Terragrunt, system design, secure train-to-cloud networking, and technical leadership across stakeholders.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly parseable: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience, simple text formatting, and no problematic tables, graphics, or columns. Relevant keywords such as Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, AWS, Linux, TLS, cert-manager, Prometheus, Grafana, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, and PostgreSQL are present and supported by the candidate information. ATS matching will likely be good for junior or mid-level DevOps, platform engineering, CI/CD, and test-infrastructure roles. Matching probability for this specific vacancy is lower because the document does not contain supported evidence for Terragrunt, mTLS, system design, practical security, virtual machines, or production cloud operations. It should not add those terms merely to improve keyword matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV shows a credible partial match. It demonstrates hands-on infrastructure engineering through GitLab CI ownership, Helm-based Kubernetes environments, Docker Compose, monitoring, ingress, TLS automation, and a Terraform-provisioned Hetzner project. AWS is represented accurately as fundamentals and personal learning. Analytical thinking and communication are supported by pipeline profiling, measurable optimisation, the internal CI onboarding guide, and mentoring two interns. The CV also shows some stakeholder value: QA and product teams use the merge-request environments for review and end-to-end testing. However, the candidate material indicates gaps against several core requirements: strong Terraform and Terragrunt, broad cloud environment design and operation, formal systems architecture/system design, mTLS, practical security awareness, production on-call or operational ownership, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, and virtual-machine experience. The CV should therefore position the candidate as an emerging DevOps/platform engineer with strong CI/CD and Kubernetes test-infrastructure experience, not as an already-established cloud infrastructure architect. No unsupported skills or experiences were detected in the document.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. MINOR ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENT — In the Professional Summary, make the scope of the candidate’s infrastructure ownership more explicit and connect it to the role’s terminology without overstating production-cloud experience. For example, change the opening to: "QA automation engineer transitioning into DevOps/platform engineering, with hands-on ownership of CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes-based test infrastructure, ephemeral environments, observability, and infrastructure automation for three product teams." Keep the existing quantified pipeline and homelab evidence.

2. MINOR ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENT — In the Odrava Health Software experience section, add the existing stakeholder and communication evidence to make the requirement about bringing stakeholders along more visible. Add a bullet such as: "Enabled QA and product teams to review features and run end-to-end tests before merge through ephemeral environments; wrote the internal CI guide used for team onboarding and mentored two QA interns in 2023." This is supported by the candidate information and avoids claiming formal cross-functional technical leadership.

3. ATS/CLARITY IMPROVEMENT — In the Technical Skills section, separate demonstrated professional experience from personal learning more visibly. Rename "Cloud learning" to "Cloud and infrastructure projects" and retain the qualifiers: "AWS fundamentals (EC2 and S3, personal learning)" and "Terraform, Hetzner VPS (personal project)." This preserves truthful keyword coverage while preventing recruiters from interpreting AWS or Terraform as production-level expertise.

4. MINOR CONTENT IMPROVEMENT — In the Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps project, state the operational design elements already present in the source material in a more recruiter-readable way: "Deployed applications from Git through Argo CD; configured Prometheus, Grafana and Loki monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS; provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and used Ansible at a basic level." This makes observability, ingress, TLS, GitOps, and infrastructure as code easier to identify during screening.

5. MINOR ATS IMPROVEMENT — In the Professional Summary or Technical Skills section, include the exact supported term "infrastructure as code" alongside Terraform, rather than implying it only through the section heading. For example: "Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform (personal project), Ansible (basic), Bash, Python." Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, or security claims because they are not supported by the candidate information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into DevOps/platform engineering. It uses quantified results effectively, including reducing pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, reducing CI runner costs by about 30%, and lowering flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The selected infrastructure projects add useful evidence of Kubernetes, GitOps, monitoring and Terraform practice. The document is professional and appropriately transparent about personal-project, learning and namespace-level experience. The main content limitation is that the target role is broader and more infrastructure-focused than the candidate's primarily test-infrastructure background.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses standard section headings, conventional chronological experience, readable bullets and searchable technology names. It contains strong keywords including GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, Linux, AWS, TLS, Prometheus, Grafana, Python and Java. AI/ATS screening probability is good for junior-to-mid DevOps, platform engineering and CI/CD infrastructure roles, but moderate for this specific contractor role because the CV does not support or demonstrate Terragrunt, mTLS, broader cloud infrastructure operation, production Kubernetes administration or system design. The explicit labels such as 'personal project,' 'basic,' 'namespace-level experience' and 'personal learning' improve credibility, although they may reduce keyword-match strength for requirements that expect professional production experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows credible hands-on infrastructure automation through GitLab CI ownership, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, Helm, Docker Compose, monitoring, GitOps and a Terraform-provisioned Hetzner project. It also demonstrates analytical thinking, clear communication and some technical leadership through pipeline profiling, onboarding documentation, mentoring and collaboration with QA and product teams. AWS fundamentals, Linux and TLS certificate automation are represented. Important role gaps remain: no Terragrunt, no mTLS experience, no demonstrated full system architecture or system-design ownership, no IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, no backend or full-stack experience, and no production AWS or equivalent cloud-platform ownership. The CV should not imply these capabilities because they are not supported by the candidate information. The strongest alignment is with a developing DevOps/platform engineer focused on CI/CD, test infrastructure and Kubernetes application environments rather than the full scope of a cloud infrastructure contractor designing train-to-cloud systems.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, include the supported seven years of experience and make the infrastructure scope more explicit without overstating it. For example, change the opening to: "QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including recent ownership of CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes-based test environments and build tooling for three product teams." Retain the existing statements about Helm, Kubernetes, GitOps, monitoring and Terraform personal projects.

2. In the Technical Skills section, add a clearly labelled collaboration/leadership line after the technical categories: "Technical leadership and communication: CI onboarding documentation, mentoring, collaboration with QA and product teams." This uses evidence already present in the Experience and Projects sections and improves matching for the requirement concerning leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along.

3. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, strengthen the existing onboarding and mentoring bullet by making its practical impact clearer without inventing a metric. Replace "Wrote an internal guide to the CI system used in team onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023" with: "Authored the internal CI-system guide used in team onboarding and mentored two QA interns in 2023." 

4. In the Technical Skills section, make the TLS evidence more ATS-searchable while remaining precise. Change "TLS certificate automation with cert-manager" to "SSL/TLS certificate automation with cert-manager." Do not add "mTLS," because the candidate information does not support mTLS experience.

5. In the Technical Skills section, preserve the current qualification labels but make the distinction between professional and personal exposure even clearer. For example, change "Terraform (personal project)" to "Terraform (personal Hetzner infrastructure project)" and change "AWS fundamentals (EC2 and S3, personal learning)" to "AWS fundamentals: EC2 and S3 (personal learning)." This helps recruiters interpret the experience accurately and avoids an assumption of professional AWS or Terraform ownership.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional CV with a clear DevOps/platform-engineering direction, credible quantified achievements, and good evidence of progression from QA automation into infrastructure work. The structure is easy to scan: summary, skills, experience, projects, education, certifications, and languages are logically ordered. The strongest content includes the reduction in pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, the 30% runner-cost reduction, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, the 900-test suite, and the reduction in flaky tests to below 2%. The CV is also appropriately careful about scope by stating namespace-level Kubernetes experience, personal Terraform work, and CKA preparation rather than claiming unsupported production-cluster ownership or certification. The main limitation is that the document is better aligned to a junior/mid-level DevOps or platform transition role than to this contractor role's expected depth in cloud architecture, Terraform/Terragrunt, security, and networking.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible. It uses standard section headings, conventional chronological experience entries, readable text formatting, and relevant keywords including Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, AWS, Linux, TLS, cert-manager, Prometheus, Grafana, and PostgreSQL. The explicit labels for personal projects and AWS learning help prevent overstatement. The contact section includes both GitLab and GitHub URLs, which is useful for a technical role. For slightly stronger matching, the CV could make the supported stakeholder-facing work more prominent and ensure consistent wording around TLS certificate management, ephemeral environments, observability, and infrastructure as code. It should not add Terragrunt, mTLS, production AWS, or broader cloud-architecture claims because those are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a credible foundation for the role: hands-on CI/CD and test-infrastructure engineering, Kubernetes and Helm usage, Terraform in a personal Hetzner project, Linux, TLS certificate automation, monitoring, analytical pipeline optimization, and communication through onboarding documentation and mentoring. It also shows relevant ownership and collaboration with product and QA teams. However, the candidate's material indicates gaps in strong Terraform/Terragrunt experience, full cloud-environment design and operation at the level implied by the engagement, mTLS, explicit practical security work, formal systems architecture/design, IoT or remote-device integration, backend/full-stack engineering, and virtual-machine experience. AWS is only shown as fundamentals/personal learning, not professional cloud operation. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than CV-writing defects. The CV is therefore a truthful but partial match, strongest for the platform/CI/CD and observability aspects of the role rather than the full fleet-connectivity architecture scope.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT 1 — In the Professional Summary, make the stakeholder and observability relevance more explicit using only existing evidence. For example, revise the final two sentences to: "Built short-lived merge-request environments using Helm and Kubernetes, improved pipeline speed and reliability through parallelisation and dependency caching, and created Grafana reporting for flaky tests by team. Documented the CI system for onboarding and supported QA and product teams in reviewing features before merge. Personal infrastructure projects include a k3s homelab with GitOps, monitoring and Terraform-provisioned Hetzner VPS infrastructure." Keep the existing namespace-level scope and CKA preparation statement.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 3 — In the Technical Skills section, change "TLS certificate automation with cert-manager" to "SSL/TLS certificate automation with cert-manager" so the document uses the job description's terminology while remaining truthful. These qualifiers are important for accurate recruiter interpretation and should not be removed or replaced with stronger wording such as "strong Terraform," "cloud engineer," or "AWS experience."
